title: When Mass Is Measured but Energy Is Analyzed: A Mass-Balance Commentary on the DiAL Health Trial Protocol
content: The DiAL Health Pilot Trial is a well-designed study that measures body mass, fat mass, fat-free mass, and food intake using state-of-the-art methods. Yet its analysis converts these mass measurements into energy equivalents and uses energy as the primary variable. This commentary identifies three loci of energy derivation in the protocol: the weight-loss nomograms, the CR adherence quantification (Equation 1), and the calorie prescription itself. A concrete numerical example shows that energy-based and mass-based analyses can produce divergent results for the same participant. The energy balance equation is mathematically underdetermined with respect to growth composition: one equation, two unknowns. The mass measurements are not. The TRE arm of the trial is not affected by the same issue, because its adherence metric is time-based rather than energy-based. This makes the CR analysis an isolated case rather than a general problem with the trial. A mass-balance analysis would preserve the information that the energy conversion discards, and would produce adherence metrics directly interpretable in the units actually measured. The argument is not that the DiAL Health trial is flawed. It is that the analytical framework it inherited contains a detour that is no longer necessary given the measurements the trial already performs.
